Inventory of Municipal Solar Ordinances Updated 2025 (Includes ESS)
officialSources.owner: Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources

records.evidenceText: State law says cities and towns tax covered renewable energy resources and associated equipment at $5.00 per AC kW for tangible property, and real property on which renewable resources are located at $3.50 per AC kW. OER rules require municipal ordinances/resolutions assessing commercial renewable tangible tax to apply the $5.00/kW formula and allow municipal waiver ordinances for some non-revenue systems. The Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources 2025 municipal solar ordinance inventory provides a municipality-by-municipality official inventory with an Adopted Tax Ordinance? column across all 39 cities/towns; it identifies tax ordinances or none-found statuses but does not replace assessor confirmation for a specific project.
records.formulaOrRateSummary: Statutory charge can be calculated as applicable_tangible_component = AC kW * $5.00 and applicable_real_property_component = AC kW * $3.50, but components must not be applied without tax-classification and assessor confirmation. Residential and manufacturer-employed renewable equipment may be exempt. Savings require counterfactual ordinary property/tangible tax minus assessor-confirmed statutory charge.
requiredInputs: system use and tax classification: residential, manufacturer-employed, commercial, REG, net-metered, virtual net-metered, other
municipal exemption or waiver ordinance status
current tax bill or assessor confirmation
serverDerivableInputs: municipal_assessor_jurisdiction from official municipal boundary join
limitations: The 2025 OER inventory is an official statewide municipal ordinance inventory, but it is not an assessor ruling or tax bill for a specific project.
Municipal code/source links still need direct row-by-row verification before importing deterministic municipality-specific tax outcomes into runtime.
User-facing dollar savings still require current assessor treatment, project classification, real/tangible applicability, pre-2017 interconnection status, and tax-bill lines.
records.nextAction: Use the OER 2025 inventory as the official municipality routing checklist; verify each linked municipal ordinance before runtime import and keep assessor/tax-bill gating for calculations.

officialSources.title: Michigan Treasury ESA: Special Millages and Renaissance Zones
2025 City of Detroit Partnership Renaissance Zone Schedule
Michigan Renaissance Zone Act CY 2023 Report
Michigan State Administrative Board March 15, 2022 Minutes
officialSources.owner: Michigan Department of Technology, Management & Budget / State Administrative Board

records.evidenceText: Detroit says Renaissance Zones are a City/Wayne/State effort and include waiver of city income and utility users taxes, most city property taxes, county property taxes, and state income/single-business tax for qualified participants physically located in a sub-zone and not delinquent. State/MEDC annual reports describe most state and local taxes, including real and personal property tax, as abated for specified years. Official annual-report search results identify active Renewable Energy Renaissance Zone evidence outside Detroit/Wayne, including Verso Quinnesec in Breitung Township/Dickinson County in 2022, and Detroit/Wayne examples such as Lynch Rd./Detroit Chassis as geographic/company subzones rather than DSIRE 3216 RERZ project-specific evidence. No official source found in this pass ties Factory ZERO or another Detroit/Wayne property to an approved DSIRE 3216 Renewable Energy Renaissance Zone package.
records.formulaOrRateSummary: Workflow only until approved-zone/company documents and actual eligible tax lines are supplied. A deterministic benefit can be calculated only from eligible otherwise-due tax lines multiplied by the approved benefit-share multiplier: 1.00 in full exemption years, then 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 during the three-year phaseout, then 0 after expiration/revocation. Do not treat ESA acquisition-cost multipliers as the benefit multiplier.
requiredInputs: approved RERZ or Renaissance Zone designation/agreement/certificate
approved local-unit resolution or abatement approval
approved zone legal description, map, or parcel list
parcel or facility confirmation inside the approved zone
zone term, final year, and current phaseout year
eligible state education tax otherwise due
eligible real property tax otherwise due
eligible personal property tax or ESA statement lines
eligible Detroit/local income tax otherwise due if claimed
excluded tax lines: special assessments, debt/bond/sinking-fund obligations, sales/use tax, Michigan CIT, non-abated obligations
serverDerivableInputs: parcel candidate from official parcel source
phaseout multiplier only after approved final year is known
limitations: Detroit/Wayne sample properties cannot be calculated from public address/parcel lookup alone.
No official public document found here proves a sample Detroit/Wayne property is in a specific approved Renewable Energy Renaissance Zone for DSIRE 3216.
Official annual reports found Detroit/Wayne geographic/company subzones and non-Detroit Renewable Energy Renaissance Zone examples, but not a Detroit/Wayne RERZ package.
Factory ZERO or Detroit-Wayne sample calculations need project-specific MSF/SAB designation, local-unit approval, legal description/parcel inclusion, and actual abated tax-line documents.
records.nextAction: Obtain approved-zone/company documents and tax bills/returns before any user-facing estimate; keep as document/accountant workflow.

officialSources.title: Quincy Municipal Code Title 5 Business Licenses and Regulations
Quincy Municipal Code Chapter 5.06 Business License
Quincy Municipal Code Chapter 3.28 Public Utility Business Tax
Washington Department of Revenue B&O Tax

records.evidenceText: Quincy Municipal Code Title 5 contains Business License, Itinerant Vendors, Special Events, Taxicabs, Yard Sales, Alcoholic Beverage Control, Admissions, Dance Permits, and Pawnbrokers chapters. QMC 5.06.020 requires a business license for engaging in business, with a de minimis exemption in QMC 5.06.025 for businesses at or below $4,000 beginning January 1, 2026 when they do not maintain a place of business in the City. QMC 3.28 imposes a Public Utility Business Tax on defined public utility businesses, at 6% for telephone/light/power/gas, 4% for domestic sewerage/refuse/water, and 1% for industrial sewer/reuse water distribution. No official Quincy source found here affirmatively states that there is no general local B&O/gross-receipts tax beyond licensing and public utility tax, so absence of a general B&O chapter is not treated as final proof of nonexistence.
records.formulaOrRateSummary: Officially supported: business-license workflow under QMC 5.06 and public utility business tax under QMC 3.28. Public utility tax = gross income from the defined public utility business in Quincy multiplied by the QMC 3.28.040 rate: telephone 6%, light/power 6% with monthly billing cap language, gas 6%, domestic sewerage 4%, refuse 4%, water 4%, industrial sewer 1%, reuse water distribution 1%. General local B&O/gross-receipts tax for non-utility business remains unproven either way from the searched official sources.
requiredInputs: official Quincy business license endorsement/account status
whether activity is a QMC 3.28 public utility business
gross income from utility business in Quincy if QMC 3.28 applies
for non-utility businesses: official city confirmation if a separate local B&O/gross-receipts tax applies
limitations: Official code proves a business-license requirement and public utility business tax.
Official code table of contents searched did not reveal a general local B&O/gross-receipts chapter, but no official no-tax confirmation was found.
Do not include non-utility Quincy local B&O in runtime totals without direct city confirmation.
records.nextAction: For runtime, implement Quincy only as a business-license/public-utility-tax routing note unless City Finance confirms no separate general B&O/gross-receipts tax or publishes a current schedule.

Manufacturing/wholesaling/retailing uses $127.40 basic per business location annually plus $7.60 per employee annually. Business services/personal services/motion picture/recreation/entertainment uses $127.40 plus $11.90 per employee. Professions and related occupations uses $127.40 plus $15.45 per employee. Unclassified uses $127.40 plus $11.90 per employee. Special schedules include contractors $1.00 per $1,000 valuation capped at $530, laundry annual tiers from $127.40 to $1,273.80, residential rentals $12.70/unit or hotels/motels $25.50/unit, commercial rentals $127.40 for first 5,000 sq ft plus $2.55 per additional 100 sq ft or fraction, and vending/coin-operated $127.40 minimum plus 1% gross receipts over $5,000.

officialSources.title: Anaheim Municipal Code 3.16.010 Services - License Tax

records.evidenceText: Anaheim Title 3 imposes license taxes on specified businesses. Chapter 3.08 gross-receipts rows set manufacturing/wholesaling, retailing, and miscellaneous at $40 if annual gross receipts are under $100,000; otherwise $0.095 per $1,000 gross receipts or $60, whichever is greater. Dwelling/hotel/motel/transient occupancy and recreation/entertainment are $40 under $100,000; otherwise $0.19 per $1,000 gross receipts or $60, whichever is greater. Chapter 3.12 professions taxes the first practicing professional principal at $135, each additional professional principal at $150, salaried/contract professional employee at $75, and other employees at $10. Chapter 3.16 services is $68 plus $10 per average employee. Chapter 3.24 contractors is $125/year for general or engineering contractors and $100/year for subcontractors/specialty contractors. Chapter 3.28 nonresidential rental, including warehousing/storage, is $0.015 per square foot of gross rental space.
records.formulaOrRateSummary: Sample-relevant rows: manufacturing/wholesale/retail/miscellaneous = gross receipts < $100,000: $40; otherwise max($60, $0.095 per $1,000 gross receipts). Hotel/lodging and recreation/entertainment = gross receipts < $100,000: $40; otherwise max($60, $0.19 per $1,000 gross receipts). Professional = $135 first professional principal + $150 additional professional principal + $75 salaried/contract professional employee + $10 other employee. Services = $68 + $10 per average employee. Contractors = $125 general/engineering or $100 subcontractor/specialty. Nonresidential rental/warehouse/storage = $0.015 per gross rental square foot.
requiredInputs: service vs professional service vs other chapter classification
processing fee and state accessibility fee applicability
limitations: Address alone can flag Anaheim applicability but not business class, gross receipts, employee count, professional principal count, contractor class, or square footage.
Regulated miscellaneous activities beyond sample-relevant classes remain workflow rows unless separately normalized.
records.nextAction: Runtime can implement extracted Title 3 sample-relevant rows with class and tax-base gates; keep other regulated permits suppressed until separately normalized.

officialSources.title: Vernon Code Chapter 5.08 Business License Tax

records.evidenceText: Vernon says business license tax depends on classification and activity level, is due before operations, renewed annually, and penalties begin after February 1. The code sets a general employee-count schedule, special warehousing square-footage tax, and special formulas for hazardous waste, waste-to-energy, recycling, and related categories. Vernon says a Special Parcel Tax is levied on non-refrigerated warehouses, truck terminals, freight terminals, and distribution facilities and collected through the property tax bill, but directs users to check the current rate with the City.
records.formulaOrRateSummary: General business license tax uses employee-count brackets. Warehousing uses $1,200 minimum for first 5,000 sq ft plus $0.21/sq ft above 5,000, capped at $11,950 per location. Hazardous waste uses 4% of inorganic hazardous waste gross receipts plus 1% of organic/infectious waste gross receipts, $5,000 minimum. Special parcel tax is lookup/tax-bill workflow because current rate is not published on the official page.
requiredInputs: warehouse square footage and apportionment if mixed use
gross receipts by hazardous waste category if applicable
tonnage or gallonage for waste/recycling special categories if applicable
facility category for special parcel tax
parcel/tax bill showing special parcel tax line
current city-confirmed special parcel tax rate
serverDerivableInputs: parcel candidate for special parcel tax routing
limitations: Address alone can flag Vernon and a possible warehouse/distribution workflow but cannot calculate without employee/square-foot/class facts.
Special parcel tax should not be calculated from address alone because the official page says to check current rate with the City and the tax is collected on the property tax bill.
Include only after user inputs or tax-bill/city confirmation are present.
records.nextAction: Implement business-license formula rows for confirmed classes; keep special parcel tax suppressed until bill/current-rate confirmation.

records.evidenceText: San Diego requires all businesses operating in the city to obtain a Business Tax Certificate, including home-based businesses and independent contractors. Annual fee is $34 for 12 or fewer employees, or $125 plus $5 per employee for 13 or more employees. Mail applications include $34 business tax plus $4 SB-1186 fee, and beginning July 1, 2025 an additional $1.47 per employee minimum wage enforcement fee. Large-business, BID, late, and other additional charges may apply.
records.formulaOrRateSummary: Base annual certificate: if employees <= 12, $34; if employees >= 13, $125 + $5 * employee count. Add $4 SB-1186 fee where applicable and $1.47 per employee minimum wage enforcement fee beginning July 1, 2025. Late: $25 or 10% after 15 days, plus 1% per month. Other assessments may apply.

limitations: Address alone can flag applicability but cannot determine employee count, BID assessment, rental-unit facts, or late fees.
